How the disease spreads (test document)

TEST FIXTURE written for automated tests. It is not official text from any health organization.

Contact with body fluids

The virus spreads through direct contact with blood, vomit, faeces, urine or other body fluids of a person who is sick or who has died from the disease.

Touching objects soiled with these fluids, such as bedding or needles, can also spread it.

What does not spread it

It is not spread through the air like influenza, and there is no evidence that mosquitoes or other insects carry it.

Safe burials

Bodies of people who died from the disease remain very contagious. Burials should be done by trained teams wearing protective equipment, and families should not wash or touch the body.
